tw-wi-hartford-bauer-1898.st: At the hearing (Milwaukee Sentinel, 7 Jun 1898) it came out that on the drive back from Holy Hill the assailant left the victim, a Milwaukee man, alone in the rig 'quite a while' at a lonely spot on the Holy Hill-Hartford road before shooting him; bail was set at $5,000.

set.t: Found and dug out; look-only. The 1894 Sanborn map (sheet 1) shows the Jno. Enes Brewery about 1/2 mile south of the post office, built against the hill beside the road up the bluff, with ice houses and a malt house; whether this was Ritter's earlier brewery is not yet confirmed, so the pin stays on the town. In 1926 the site was called the old Ritter brewery ruins; whether it is the 'Jno. Enes Brewery' of the 1894 Sanborn is unconfirmed (Enes may have been Ritter's successor). The 1880 census confirms an Enes brewery: John Enes, 53, and Christian Enes, 25, brewers, alongside Joseph Ritter, 52, and Albert Miller, 27, also brewers, so Henderson had two brewing families.

set.st: "Old Whit" Knaggs, one of the county's first settlers, kept a trading post and was said to have gathered gold from land speculators; he buried it along the Shiawassee River just south of Knaggs' Bridge. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself. Knaggs' hill is on the E (right) bank; Gaylord Cemetery adjoins it: look-only near the cemetery. 1873 atlas places the crossing beside the Shiawassee treaty reserve. 1936: Knaggs gully near the bridge, dug over many times. The earliest telling found (Michigan Pioneer and Historical Collections, 1902) says Whitmore Knaggs buried speculators' money around Knaggs Bridge on the Shiawassee. A man named Hadd dug for it about twenty years later, and before the Civil War parties dug at night by a map that marked 'the rock, the tree, and the spring' (E. O. Byam showed them the spring). It names storekeeper Thomas B. Allen, and says the post site then belonged to Hon. N. G. Phillips.

tw-wi-milwaukee-scholl-homestead-pot-191.st: His probate (1886) calls him a moneylender: $1,066 in currency was found in the house, and the inventory lists no gold, so the 1915 pot was outside the estate.
